Tango takes center stage in the evening. The dance is popular worldwide, but Argentina has one indisputable distinction: it was born here. The remarkable world of tango unfolds on stage, where passion and virtuosity evoke love and elegance. Tango originated around the city's ports among poor immigrants, gaucho herders, and other people struggling to find their place. At first, two men danced it in a rather uninhibited style, and its name was associated with the Latin word *tangere*, meaning “to touch.” Over time, tango slowed down and acquired a more intimate character. Tango orchestras appeared, and the dance rapidly gained popularity. Today it is among the most sensual dances in the world, conveying sincerity, gallantry, and tenderness. The restaurant's interior sets the mood, while a menu of several traditional courses and excellent Argentine wines adds to the romance of the evening. Be sure to try mate, too!

## Tango Show at La Ventana

Enjoy a memorable tango show and dinner at La Ventana Tango House. The captivating rhythms of this passionate dance and the couples performing it will leave a lasting impression, as will the traditional Argentine dinner, with drinks included. A private transfer and the services of a Russian-speaking guide are included. Pickup from your hotel takes place between 19:00 and 19:30, depending on its location. Dinner begins at 20:00. The two-hour show runs from 21:00 to 23:00. After the show, a transfer takes you back to your hotel, arriving by 23:45.

## Price

The excursion costs from $145. The exact rate is confirmed at booking.

Duration: 4 hours • Start: 9:00–9:30 a.m. • Languages: English and Spanish

Today begins with a guided walking tour of Oaxaca's historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site rich in color and centuries of culture. Explore the magnificent Church of Santo Domingo, a masterpiece of Baroque architecture. Stroll along the lively Andador Turístico, lined with artisan shops, galleries, and cafés. Visit the Zócalo, Oaxaca's main square, and experience its vibrant local life. Your knowledgeable guide will share insights into the city's colonial history, pre-Hispanic heritage, and living cultural traditions. After the tour, enjoy free time or choose optional activities: a cooking class, visits to local art galleries, or a tasting of locally produced mezcal.

Tour highlights: ● Discover the Church of Santo Domingo, one of Mexico's most iconic churches.

● Walk the colorful streets of Oaxaca's colonial center.

● Learn about the Zapotec and Mixtec heritage, colonial influences, and present-day traditions.

Visit lively markets and squares full of local life and artisan treasures, accompanied by a certified bilingual guide.

Included: Shared transportation, certified bilingual guide, admission to historical sites.

Not included: Meals, admission to optional attractions, tips, personal expenses.

## A Full Day in São Paulo

São Paulo reveals itself gradually. Beyond the traffic and high-rise buildings lie historic streets, cultural centers, and neighborhoods with their own ways of life. The city was shaped by people from many countries, a diversity reflected in its architecture, food, and storefront signs. A full day offers a closer look at this varied urban environment.

Well-known landmarks include the MASP museum, Ibirapuera Park, and Liberdade, a district associated with Japanese immigration. Historic architecture and modern buildings tell different chapters of São Paulo's development. These are examples of what the city offers; visits to individual museums and districts depend on the agreed itinerary.

The sightseeing tour lasts 8 hours and is ideal for travelers who want to discover the fascinating city behind São Paulo's business reputation. Notice the details: an old façade between modern towers, a street sign, or the window of a small café. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended.

## Excursion Terms

The excursion costs $183 per person.

Discounts may be available for more than one traveler; contact us to discuss.

## Your First Look at Santiago

The historic center grew around Plaza de Armas. Here you will find the cathedral and buildings connected with the country's government and the city's history. On nearby streets, architecture from different periods stands alongside shops, cafés, and pedestrian areas. Discovering this part of Santiago is a fine beginning to a trip around Chile.

It is fascinating to look around the city and watch its buildings change from old façades to modern towers. The landmarks mentioned here help introduce Santiago; the exact stops and building visits are determined by the agreed excursion itinerary. Comfortable footwear and sun protection are useful for the walk.

## Excursion Terms

The excursion costs $80 per person.
